To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) The free energy of intercalation of a drug in DNA can be calculated using a molecular dynamics free energy perturbation method, (b) The calculated free energy differences between different base pair sequences are in good agreement with the experimental results, and (c) The results are encouraging for the development of a general method for the prediction of the specificity of drug –DNA interactions.
the free energy differences calculated by our method are in qualitative agreement with experimental results and that this agreement is not surprising given the simplicity of our model.

the free energy of binding of daunomycin is strongly sequence dependent, with the highest affinity for the sequence 5′‐CGCG‐3′, and that the free energy change for the binding of 9‐ammoniumacridine is also sequence dependent, with a preference for sequences containing G and T, in agreement with the experimental results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of free energy perturbations methods to study drug‐DNA interactions.
the calculation of the free energy of binding between a drug and DNA.
the development of computational methods to study drug–DNA interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present model is capable of describing correctly the base specificity of the binding of acridine derivatives and daunomycins to DNA.
, while the results obtained here are encouraging, further studies, including the effects of solvent, are needed in order to fully understand the binding of these drugs to DNA.
the free energy perturbation method, when combined with molecular dynamics, is an efficient tool for studying the specificity of drug – nucleic acid interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the molecular mechanics approach is able to reproduce the trends of the base sequence preference of intercalators, and that it is a promising tool for the study of the base specificity of drug–DNA interactions.
the free energy perturbation method can provide a reliable estimate for the free energy difference in drug–DNA interactions.

, although the molecular mechanics force fields used in this study are not sufficiently accurate to reproduce the experimental free energy differences between DNA · drug complexes, the trends observed are qualitatively correct.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method is able to reproduce the experimentally observed sequence‐dependent binding of drugs, which is a result of subtle changes in the electrostatic interactions.
the method can be used to predict the base sequence preference of intercalating drugs.
free energy perturbation calculations can be used to study the specificity of drug binding to DNA.
